newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares gains on dlr short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares gains on dlr short-covering.

text.p: The Mexican peso ceded some of the initial ground it had gained by mid-morning trade on Wednesday as delaers took advantage of a firm peso to cover short-dollar positions to hedge against possible strong U.S. consumer price data expected on Thursday, traders said.
"The peso will have a very strong resistance at 7.88 per dollar until May 20, as dealers will not risk going short (on dollars) before the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were both 1.4 centavos firmer at 7.8930/7.8950 and 7.8890/7.8920 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed 1.6 centavos firmer at 7.8860/7.8890 per dollar.
"There is the possibility the FOMC will not raise U.S. rates, but you can never be completely sure," another trader said.
